source: Two externally authored hero assets, imported 2026-09-18 by tools/import_tree_isle.py for the tree-of-life-floating-island project (ADR-338).
license: Not recorded for either asset. The Tree of Life was generated for this project by the owner's Blender pipeline; the floating island was supplied by the owner and carries no licence text. Fill this in before either is distributed outside the project.
regenerate: /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/Resources/5.2/python/bin/python3.13 tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py --in assets/treeisle/tree-of-life-hero.glb --out assets/treeisle   (the five tree-glowmere-*.glb the scene loads). The two older files are made by /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender --background --python tools/import_tree_isle.py -- --island ~/Desktop/Island --tree ~/Desktop/tree_mdl/hero_pass --out assets/treeisle

assets.name: tree-of-life-hero
assets.upAxis: Y (glTF; the source .blend is Z-up and the Blender exporter converted it)
assets.note: The static hero snapshot, 3.16 M triangles across seven meshes and seven materials, with no textures and no UVs: every surface is a flat PBR factor. The source's own validation.json calls it a 'Mature static snapshot; simple PBR, no shader baking or growth export', and it means it -- the Glowmere look in hero_pass/renders/Glowmere.png is a Blender shading setup that did not survive this export. Only one of the seven materials carries any emission at all. A scene cannot restore it -- a `material` block on a `kind: "gltf"` node is parsed and dropped -- so tree-of-life-hero-glowmere.glb does, and that is what the scene loads. See docs/decisions/ADR-338.

assets.name: tree-of-life-hero-glowmere
assets.conversion: tools/glowmere_tree_materials.py rewrites the GLB's seven material definitions to the Glowmere palette read off hero_pass/renders/Glowmere.png, and copies the binary chunk through unchanged -- it verifies the copy's SHA-256 against the hero's and refuses to write if it moved. The vertex data of this file is not merely equivalent to the hero's, it is the same bytes.
assets.note: The variant the scene actually loads. A `material` block on a `kind: "gltf"` node is parsed and then dropped with a warning, so a scene cannot restore a palette the export dropped; the only levers it has on a glTF node are `emissiveBoost` and `roughnessScale`, and boosting emission on leaves that emit nothing multiplies zero. Brief §15's 'minimum required conversion'.

assets.name: floating-isle
assets.sourceFormat: fbx (Kaydara binary 7400, 3ds Max 2023, authored as FloatingHouse_v3.fbx)
assets.conversion: Blender 5.2.1 LTS FBX import -> glTF export, with all nine Unity URP materials rebuilt from FloatingIsleTextures/: BaseMap as base colour, Normal as the normal map, and the MaskMap repacked into a glTF ORM texture (occlusion from its G, roughness from 1 - its A, metallic from its R). The .mat files themselves are Unity YAML and are not importable; the mapping is written down in tools/import_tree_isle.py.
assets.upAxis: Y (converted from the source's Z-up on export)
assets.note: Everything the artist built: the landmass and grass plus a house, roof, chimney, windmill, fence, staircase and decor. The house's windows are emissive, tinted by Unity's HDR _EmissionColor (2.27, 4.87, 0.59).

assets.name: floating-isle-bare
assets.conversion: The same import, exported with only the landmass objects selected. A second export, not an edit: nothing is removed from the FBX, and floating-isle.glb still carries every object.
assets.note: The island with nobody living on it. Kept because the built structures compete with the Tree of Life for the frame -- at the scene's island scale the cottage is taller than the tree. See docs/decisions/ADR-338.

assets.name: tree-glowmere-tracery
assets.conversion: tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py. POSITION and NORMAL are memcpy'd out of the hero's binary chunk and their SHA-256 re-checked against the source after the file is written, so no vertex can move. Index buffers ARE rewritten -- that is how one primitive becomes several -- and the check there is that the triangle count is conserved exactly.
assets.note: Brief §8 'major luminous structures'. The blend's HERO | light beneath fractured bark: base [0.025, 0.10, 0.08], emission strength 1.92 on a 3D-noise mask, emission colour a height ramp from green-cyan at the roots through teal to hot orange at the crown. Split into 4 height bands x {lit, dark}; the lit fraction is 0.470 against Blender's noise(2.6, detail 3) > 0.53.

assets.name: tree-glowmere-twigs
assets.conversion: tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py. POSITION and NORMAL are memcpy'd out of the hero's binary chunk and their SHA-256 re-checked against the source after the file is written, so no vertex can move. Index buffers ARE rewritten -- that is how one primitive becomes several -- and the check there is that the triangle count is conserved exactly.
assets.note: Brief §8 'secondary glow'. The blend gives the twigs the same non-emissive wood material as the trunk, so the faint sapwood glow on 12% of the surface is an AV Gen-native addition, not an extraction -- declared as such in tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py.

assets.name: tree-glowmere-foliage
assets.conversion: tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py. POSITION and NORMAL are memcpy'd out of the hero's binary chunk and their SHA-256 re-checked against the source after the file is written, so no vertex can move. Index buffers ARE rewritten -- that is how one primitive becomes several -- and the check there is that the triangle count is conserved exactly.
assets.note: Brief §8 'foliage', and the whole reason this split exists. Blender drives both the leaf colour and the leaf emission from ObjectInfo.Random, which is per *instance*; the export preserved the instancing as contiguous 18-vertex blocks, so instance = vertex // 18 recovers it exactly. 51633 + 122767 leaves, of which 5.9% and 6.1% come out lit -- Blender's threshold is Random > 0.94. 6 height bands x {lit, dim} per mesh.

assets.name: tree-glowmere-lumens
assets.conversion: tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py. POSITION and NORMAL are memcpy'd out of the hero's binary chunk and their SHA-256 re-checked against the source after the file is written, so no vertex can move. Index buffers ARE rewritten -- that is how one primitive becomes several -- and the check there is that the triangle count is conserved exactly.
assets.note: Brief §8 'special organisms'. HERO | copper caps and pale luminous gills keys both base colour and emission off Geometry.Normal.Z < -0.25 -- the gills glow, the caps do not. Blender's Z is the GLB's Y. 61.2% of the mushroom triangles and 33.3% of the lantern triangles face down.
assets.role: special organisms: bark fungi and seed lanterns (brief §8)

assets.name: tree-glowmere-wood
assets.conversion: tools/glowmere_tree_layers.py. POSITION and NORMAL are memcpy'd out of the hero's binary chunk and their SHA-256 re-checked against the source after the file is written, so no vertex can move. Index buffers ARE rewritten -- that is how one primitive becomes several -- and the check there is that the triangle count is conserved exactly.
assets.note: Brief §8 'dark areas'. GLOWMERE | mineral charcoal, old plates and sapwood, whose Emission Strength is 0.0 -- the trunk, roots and boughs do not glow, and that is what makes the rest read. 4 noise bands off Color Ramp.001; roughness 0.58 + 0.32 * noise.

note: The scene loads the five tree-glowmere-*.glb layers, not tree-of-life-hero-glowmere.glb. The single-file variant is kept because examples/treeisland/_compare-original.* -- the 'before' arm of this pass -- is ADR-338 unchanged and still loads it.
